title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Following a regional failover incident (incident ENG-1387) we observed the SLO enforcer entering a backoff ordering race that caused cross-region thrashing and excessive load-shedding. Root cause: enforcer backoff state updates were not strictly monotonic under concurrent regional failover sequences, allowing older backoff epochs to overwrite newer decisions during a brief synchronization window. This led to cascading backoff resets and repeated load-shedding across regions. Solution: Ensure deterministic, monotonic backoff epoch semantics and atomic updates to enforcer state. Changes include 1) attach a monotonic epoch token to each backoff decision and enforce epoch compare-and-swap when applying updates, 2) add a small hysteresis window and smoothing of backoff transitions to prevent rapid flip-flopping, 3) reduce lock hold time by batching metadata writes and using pipelined Redis operations to avoid N+1 updates, 4) add prioritized per-region queueing so regional failover decisions are applied in a controlled order, 5) expose metrics for backoff_epoch, backoff_applied, and backoff_drops to aid postmortem and alerting. Testing and rollout: added unit and integration tests that reproduce the race, run the new integration/regional_failover_test in CI, and deployed behind a feature flag. Canary rollout configured for region-us-west-2 with autoscaling disabled for the canary hosts. Rollback path: flip the feature flag to off which instantly reverts to previous enforcer behavior. Checklist: - [x] reproduce race in integration test harness - [x] add monotonic epoch compare-and-swap and tests - [x] add smoothing/hysteresis logic - [x] add metrics and dashboards wiring - [x] feature-flagged canary deploy + 30m observation - [x] update runbook and rollback steps. Related: ENG-1387, ENG-1402. Impact: urgent reliability hotfix to prevent SLO violations during future regional failovers.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: The CAS approach looks correct, but I'm concerned about a potential N+1 when we iterate regions to apply updates. Can we pipeline the write?

release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilized SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failovers to prevent cross-region thrashing and spurious load-shedding. Added monotonic epoch CAS, hysteresis smoothing, pipelined metadata writes, and observability metrics. Rollout behind feature flag.
notes_for_oncall: If SLO regressions are observed after rollout, flip feature flag 'slo-enforcer-backoff-epoch' to off; monitor metrics: slo.enforcer.backoff_epoch, slo.enforcer.backoff_applied, slo.enforcer.backoff_drops, region.request_queue_length. Post-rollback run integration/regional_failover_test and collect enforcer logs (INFO level enabled for 30m).
